title: 2008 AMC 8 Problem 20
statement: The students in Mr. Neatkin’s class took a penmanship test. Two-thirds of the boys and \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the girls passed the test, and an equal number of boys and girls passed the test. What is the minimum possible number of students in the class?

solutions.text:
Let \(p\) be the common number of boys and girls who passed.

Since \(\dfrac{2}{3}\) of the boys passed, the number of boys is \(\dfrac{3p}{2}\). Since \(\dfrac{3}{4}\) of the girls passed, the number of girls is \(\dfrac{4p}{3}\).

The smallest positive \(p\) that makes both counts whole is \(6\). Then there are \(9\) boys and \(8\) girls, for a minimum total of \(17\) students.

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: Let the common number of passing boys and passing girls be \(p\).
Then total boys and girls are \(\frac{3p}{2}\) and \(\frac{4p}{3}\), so choose the smallest \(p\) that makes both whole.
